The main takeaway from our work is that
the terminal Eocene cooling and associated planktonic extinction event is a global phenomenon, but its expression in southern Australia was strongly modified by regional factors.
the Eocene/Oligocene transition in the southern Australia paleoshelf region was not a single event but rather a complex sequence of events that occurred over several hundred thousand years.
paleoceanographic reconstructions of the Eocene-Oligence boundary in southern Australia are not necessarily representative of the global ocean.
